_comment: Hand-written table for provider_lambda. Contract: `.claude/skills/lease/references/contract.md`
'Shape resolution' — and specifically its rule 'Put in the table only what the API will not
tell you'.
THIS TABLE IS THE OPPOSITE SHAPE FROM `machines_nebius.json`, FOR THE SAME REASON. Lambda's
`instance-types` endpoint returns `price_cents_per_hour`, gpu count, vCPU and host RAM live,
so none of those are here and `capacity` labels its price `verified` rather than `claim`. What
no Lambda API returns is compute capability, a human GPU name, and per-GPU memory — so that is
all this file carries. A hand-copied price here would be a second author for a value that
already has one, and the stale copy is the one that gets read.
‼️ EVERY `arch` HERE IS A `claim`. The names below were transcribed from Lambda's published
type list, not measured on a box this repo has run. `arch` is a hard admission check — a wrong
value either refuses a machine that would have worked or admits one whose kernels will not
load — so nothing may read `verified` until a job has actually been built and run for it here.
Promote a row only after that happens, one row at a time.
‼️ A TYPE NOT LISTED HERE IS NOT A TYPE THAT DOES NOT EXIST. `capacity` reports unlisted
types under `untabled_types` instead of dropping them, because an unlisted machine cannot pass
the `arch` check and a silent omission would read as 'Lambda does not sell that card'. When
that list is non-empty, this file is behind the provider — add the row, don't widen the filter.

gpu_1x_a10.note: the cheapest GPU box; the right pick when the GPU is irrelevant and the job is bound by host RAM

gpu_8x_v100.note: Volta — predates bf16; a recipe assuming bf16 autocast fails here rather than running slowly

gpu_1x_gh200.note: ‼️ the host is aarch64, so an x86 wheel set does not apply. `arch` passing is not the same as the environment being installable — that check is `env_snapshot`'s, not this field's

gpu_8x_b200_sxm.note: Blackwell — a torch built for cu121 will not load here; see the contract's arch paragraph

_comment_credential_ttl: 0 = non-expiring static API key, and this is the one place Lambda is STRONGER than the
federated-SSO provider beside it. Money rule 5 refuses a job longer than the credential
TTL; on Nebius a 30-hour training run is refused because a 12-hour token cannot reach,
monitor or destroy the box for the second half of it. Here there is no such ceiling.
_comment_tags: ‼️ `true`, but through a WEAKER CHANNEL than a label, and the weakness has to be read.
This API has no label or tag field at all — the only writable per-instance string is the
`name`, set at create. So the tag rides in the name, which means `sweep`'s tag filter is
matching on a field a human can edit in the console. A renamed box silently drops out of
every tag-filtered sweep while it goes on billing.
fleet.md 'Group by id, never by name' is about JOINS ACROSS TIME and still holds: nothing
here groups by name, and every join keys on the instance id. What the name carries is
OWNERSHIP, and it carries it forgeably. That is why `leases.json` bears more weight on this
provider than on one with real labels, and it is compounded by `history` being unsupported:
when the name has been edited, there is no second record to recover the truth from.
_comment_native_ttl: false — and unlike every other provider, the guest-side fallback the contract offers is not
merely partial here, it is INVERTED. A Lambda instance has no stopped state: it exists or it
is terminated, and it bills for existing. `shutdown -h +N` therefore stops nothing and
removes the ssh access that was the last way to release the box by hand.
So the only real dead-man switch is one that calls the terminate endpoint FROM the box,
which needs an API key on rented hardware. provider_lambda installs a systemd timer that
does exactly that, and `up` REFUSES when no `dead_man_key_path` is configured — renting a
machine that can never expire is the outcome Money rule 3 exists to prevent, and refusing
is the only alternative to it. Give it a key you are willing to have on a box a stranger
gets next; `dead_man_key_path` is deliberately separate from `api_key_path` so that is a
decision rather than a side effect.
_comment_billing_granularity: null = nobody measured it. Not zero, not one hour. Lambda's published terms have changed
on this point, and a granularity written down from memory would make every `accrued` figure
wrong in a direction nobody could see.

_comment: THE SECOND METER, and on this provider it is the ONLY residual one. Terminating an instance
releases its local disk with it — that disk is not a separate resource here, which is the
opposite of Nebius, where `instance delete` taking the boot disk is itself the hazard.
What survives is a FILESYSTEM: created and deleted independently, billed while it exists,
and attached to no instance once the box is gone. `sweep` enumerates them for that reason.
price null, as with the Nebius table: Lambda bills filesystems per GB-month and publishes
no per-hour rate through this API. null means nobody wrote it down and NEVER means free —
`lease.py` counts an unpriced row and reports the total as a lower bound.

_comment_no_image: No `image_family` key, and its absence is a fact rather than an omission: the launch API
takes region, instance type, ssh keys, filesystems, quantity and name — nothing else. There
is no image selection and no user-data field, so this adapter cannot inject anything at
create time and must ssh in after the box is reachable to arm its expiry. That ordering is
why `up` polls to reachable before it can honour Money rule 3 at all.
